reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel measurable structure, and let I be any finite index type. Let V:E->R be C^2 and kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa. Assume for every x,v in E that
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,c,epsilon with 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E x E, and fix xstar in E with grad V(xstar)=0. Fix h,M,S>=0, and assume that the function (x,r) -> ||x-xstar||^2+||r||^2 is integrable under nu with integral at most M. Let t:I->R satisfy |t_i|<=1 for every i, and omega:I x I->R satisfy sum_j |omega_ij|<=S for every i. Let b,d:I->R be arbitrary deterministic real arrays, denoting positionWeight and momentumWeight.
Write D=dim_R E, a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), G for the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on E, gi=product_I G, gamma=(G x G) x (gi x gi), and mu=nu x gamma. Thus, under mu, an incoming state (x,r) of law nu is independent of mutually independent standard Gaussian vectors u,v and independent standard Gaussian arrays xi,xi-prime. Define the exact constants
  MR=M+(1-exp(-h))D,
  B=6 MR+3 epsilon^2+3 eta D,
  C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c).
Then there exist measurable p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  run(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1).
The exact-real interpreter returns none at zero fuel. With positive fuel it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta g(x), and returns (x,1) if ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. Otherwise it recurses from next with one less fuel and adds one to a successful returned count. Thus the displayed run equality records a successful run initialized at y, with fuel and reported gradient-test count both N(y)+1, including the final successful test.
For these same witnesses, for w=((x,r),((u,v),(xi,xi-prime))) define
  P0(w)=a r+sigma u,
  Y0_i(w)=x+t_i P0(w),
  Z0_j(w)=grad V(q(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)xi_j),
  Y1_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j(w),
  Z1_j(w)=grad V(q(Y1_j(w))+sqrt(eta)xi-prime_j),
  Phi(w)=(x+h P0(w)-sum_j b_j Z1_j(w),
          a(P0(w)-sum_j d_j Z1_j(w))+sigma v).
Then Phi is jointly measurable, and there exists a Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E such that for every incoming state s,
  K(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma.
In addition, for every i in I, all of the following hold with integration over w under mu:
  ||grad V(Y0_i)||^2 is integrable,
  integral ||grad V(Y0_i)||^2 dmu <= 2 MR,
  N(Y0_i)+1 is integrable,
  integral (N(Y0_i)+1) dmu <= C[1+log(1+sqrt(2 MR)/epsilon)],
  ||grad V(Y1_i)||^2 is integrable,
  integral ||grad V(Y1_i)||^2 dmu <= 4 MR+2 S^2 B,
  N(Y1_i)+1 is integrable,
  integral (N(Y1_i)+1) dmu <= C[1+log(1+sqrt(4 MR+2 S^2 B)/epsilon)].
Counts are cast to the reals in integrability and integral statements. Integrability is Bochner integrability, and all sums range over the entire finite index type. Each K(s) is a probability measure, with measurable dependence on s for every measurable output event. The theorem supplies these witnesses, the transition kernel, and these per-index input-gradient moment and interpreter-count bounds. It does not assert an invariant law, sampler convergence, final-state moment or bias bound, or an overall algorithmic gradient-call bound including the Z0 and Z1 evaluations.
objects: The spaces E and finite I; potential V, Hessian quadratic form and gradient; kappa,eta,c,epsilon,h,M,S; incoming state law nu and stationary point xstar; deterministic arrays t,omega,b,d; measurable implicit-solution map p, approximate map q and natural-valued interpreter count witness N; standard Gaussian law G and array law gi; independent noise law gamma and state/noise law mu; constants MR,B,C; stage variables P0,Y0,Z0,Y1,Z1; joint update Phi and probability-valued Markov kernel K.
domains: E is a normed additive commutative group, real inner-product space, complete and finite-dimensional over R, with a measurable structure satisfying BorelSpace. I is any Fintype, potentially empty. V:E->R; kappa is a nonnegative real; eta,c,epsilon,h,M,S are real. nu is a probability measure on E x E and xstar belongs to E. t,b,d:I->R; omega:I->I->R. p,q:E->E; N:E->N. Noise z belongs to (E x E) x ((I->E) x (I->E)); w belongs to (E x E) x that noise space; gamma and mu are the associated product measures. Phi maps w to E x E and K has both state spaces E x E.
quantifiers: For every admissible E,I,V,kappa,eta,c,epsilon,nu,xstar,h,M,S,t,omega,b,d satisfying the listed assumptions, there exist single global p,q,N that are measurable and satisfy the implicit-equation, approximation and run conditions for every y in E. For these same witnesses there exists a Markov K with its pushforward equality for every incoming s in E x E. The two groups of integrability and moment/count inequalities each hold for every i in I. The Hessian hypothesis is for every x,v; the t and row-sum hypotheses are for every i. No witness is separately selected for individual states or indices.
assumptions: V is C^2, 1<=kappa with kappa nonnegative, and kappa^(-1)||v||^2<=D^2 V(x)[v,v]<=||v||^2 universally in x,v. Parameters satisfy 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. nu has total mass one; grad V(xstar)=0; h,M,S are nonnegative. The squared incoming distance-plus-momentum norm is integrable under nu and has integral <=M. For every i, |t_i|<=1 and sum_j |omega_ij|<=S. Final output weights b,d are arbitrary real arrays; no sign, normalization, accuracy, stability or order condition is imposed on them. The Gaussian measures are centered with identity covariance; products encode the stated independence. No Gaussian assumption is made on nu.
conclusion: There exist measurable p,q,N satisfying the global implicit equation, epsilon approximation and exact successful-run equality. The explicitly defined update Phi is jointly measurable and its gamma pushforward for every incoming state forms a Markov kernel. Under mu=nu x gamma, each first-stage input Y0_i has integrable squared-gradient norm with mean <=2 MR and integrable real count N(Y0_i)+1 with mean <=C(1+log(1+sqrt(2 MR)/epsilon)). Each second-stage input Y1_i has integrable squared-gradient norm with mean <=4 MR+2 S^2 B and integrable real count N(Y1_i)+1 with mean <=C(1+log(1+sqrt(4 MR+2 S^2 B)/epsilon)). Exact MR,B,C and all stage formulas are given in reconstructed_theorem_text.
scopes: Kernel measurability and probability laws concern every incoming state, while the quantitative integral bounds concern the particular state law nu combined with independent Gaussian noise. The bounds are per index and concern unshifted inputs Y0_i and Y1_i to the interpreter, not the shifted probe locations q(Y0_i)+sqrt(eta)xi_i or q(Y1_i)+sqrt(eta)xi-prime_i. N+1 includes the terminal interpreter gradient test; it does not by itself count the separately displayed Z0/Z1 evaluations or total calls over indices. The p/q/N witnesses work globally for all y, with no uniform pointwise bound on N asserted. The theorem does not assert a final-output moment estimate, invariant distribution, convergence rate, or numerical bias/error bound for Phi.
constant_dependencies: D=finrank_R E, MR=M+(1-exp(-h))D, B=6 MR+3 epsilon^2+3 eta D, and C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c), exactly. The first-stage bounds depend on MR,epsilon,C; second-stage bounds additionally depend on S and B. Thus eta,D,h,M,c,epsilon,S enter displayed bounds as specified; kappa does not appear explicitly outside assumptions. The bound does not explicitly use b,d or individual coefficient values t,omega beyond their supplied inequalities. a,sigma depend only on h; sqrt(eta) depends on eta. The law gamma depends on E and I; mu also depends on nu. All data precede witness existence, so the statement syntax permits witness dependence on all fixed data and asserts no reduced dependence set. 0<c<1 follows from the parameter assumptions, ensuring -log c>0.
